title: Maximum Length of Subarray With Positive Product
statement: You are given an integer array `nums`. Consider every subarray, meaning a block of consecutive elements (the empty block counts too), and multiply its elements together. Return the length of the longest block whose product is strictly greater than zero. A block containing a `0` never qualifies, so if no non-empty block has a positive product the answer is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

Only the signs matter: a product is positive when the block has no zero and an even number of negatives. Trying every block and tracking its sign is O(n²). Instead, walk left to right and remember, for blocks that **end at the current element**, the longest one with a positive product and the longest one with a negative product. A new element either keeps each sign (positive number), swaps them (negative number) or wipes both (zero).

## Approach

1. Keep `positive` and `negative`: the longest block ending here with that sign of product (`0` means none). Keep `best`, the answer.
2. On `0`, no block can end here, so reset both to `0`.
3. On a positive `num`, a positive block just grows by one; a negative block grows only if one existed.
4. On a negative `num`, the signs swap: a previous negative block becomes positive (if it existed), and any previous positive block, even the empty one, becomes negative with one more element.
5. After each element, update `best` with `positive` and return it at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, -2, -3, 4]`.

- `1`: `positive = 1`, `negative = 0`, `best = 1`.
- `-2`: the old positive `1` becomes `negative = 2`; there was no negative block, so `positive = 0`.
- `-3`: the old negative `2` becomes `positive = 3`; the old positive `0` gives `negative = 1`. `best = 3`.
- `4`: `positive = 4`, `negative = 2`, `best = 4`. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n), one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(1), only three counters.

## Pitfalls

- Never multiply the values: products of up to 10^5 numbers of size 10^9 overflow everywhere. Track signs only.
- On a negative number, save the old `positive` before overwriting it; both new values depend on the old pair.
- A negative block of length `0` does not exist, so extending it must stay `0`, not become `1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `positive` | longest block ending at the current element with a positive product |
| `negative` | longest block ending at the current element with a negative product |
| `previousPositive` | `positive` before the current negative element swapped the signs |
| `best` | longest positive block seen so far |
| `num` | the current element |

narration.2: No block ends before the array starts, so there is no positive block yet.
narration.3: Likewise there is no negative block yet.
narration.4: best holds the longest positive block found anywhere so far.
narration.6: Visit the elements from left to right, extending blocks that end here.
narration.7: A zero makes every product through it zero.
narration.8: So no positive block can end at this element...
narration.9: ...and no negative block either; start over after it.
narration.10: A positive number keeps the sign of whatever block it extends.
narration.11: The positive block grows by one; the empty block plus this number is positive too.
narration.12: A negative block grows by one only if one already existed.
narration.14: A negative number swaps the signs, so keep the old positive length first.
narration.15: An existing negative block times a negative number turns positive and grows by one.
narration.16: Any positive block, even the empty one, becomes negative and grows by one.
narration.18: Record the longest positive block that ends here.
narration.20: Return the longest positive block seen during the scan.
